key_insight: Prior support for target concepts is highly uneven, so SFT works better when instruction selection adapts to the long-tail “prior barrier” instead of using uniform supervision.
engineering_relevance: For LLM fine-tuning pipelines, PASS suggests a budget-aware way to allocate labels or instructions toward undercovered concepts, improving downstream performance under limited annotation budgets.
method: Defines “prior barrier” to measure how much pretrained support competes against the target concept.
Builds reference-derived concepts and estimates the distinguishing evidence each instruction provides.
Adaptively reallocates selection budget to concepts still insufficiently covered under current supervision.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that PASS outperforms seven state-of-the-art instruction selection methods across four backbone-budget settings, with ablations showing adaptive allocation is better than uniform allocation.
watch_item: The approach depends on estimating prior barriers and instruction evidence accurately, which may be sensitive to backbone choice, task distribution, and reference concept quality.
paper_title: Overcoming Prior Barriers: Supervised Fine-Tuning under Long-Tail Distribution
